newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech sees CZK 160 mln 96 gross profit.
newsitem.headline: Czech sees CZK 160 mln 96 gross profit.

text.p: Czech engineering concern Skoda Praha a.s. on Wednesday said it expected its 1996 gross profit to rise sharply to 160 million crowns, from 26 million the previous year.
Skoda Praha spokesman Milan Kuchta added that the firm expects to pay a 30 crown per share dividend for 1996, up from 20 crowns per share for 1995.
Kuchta said the rise could be attributed in large part to one-off payments made in 1995, that negatively affected the firm's bottom line that year.
"Before last year, some changes to contracts due to changing economic laws forced some payments which we never had before...and do not have now," Kuchta said.
He did not elaborate on the payments.
The main shareholders of Skoda Praha include the state privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (54.7 percent), investment firm SIS (15.5 percent), and investment firm ATC (14.9 percent).
Skoda Praha sahres dipped 15 crowns on the Prague Stock Exchange on Wednesday to 1,075.
